annotations.description: GPT5 Story failed to block the attacking Thraben Inspector (1/2) with Kami of Ancient Law (2/2). Kami would have killed the Inspector and survived at 2/1 remaining toughness. This was a free profitable block that removes the opponent's creature.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timed out), did not block — took 1 damage and let Thraben Inspector survive.
annotations.betterLine: Block Thraben Inspector with Kami of Ancient Law. Kami kills the Inspector and survives, removing the opponent's creature for free.

annotations.description: Cast Drag Under before playing the Plains land drop. Since Drag Under draws a card, playing the land first preserves more flexibility: after resolving Drag Under, having 4 lands means they could leave Thriving Isle untapped (for blue mana) instead of just the new Plains (white only), allowing them to potentially cast Spectral Sailor or hold up blue mana based on what they draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Drag Under before playing Plains land
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, then cast Drag Under using Island + original Plains + Thriving Isle, keeping the new Plains or Thriving Isle untapped for more flexible mana after seeing the drawn card.

annotations.description: Opponent has zero creatures on the battlefield and all lands are tapped, meaning there are no blockers and no instant-speed interaction possible. Attacking with only Merfolk Pupil instead of both creatures leaves 1 free damage on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Merfolk Pupil (1 damage)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Merfolk Pupil and Gideon's Lawkeeper) for 2 damage, since the opponent has no creatures and all lands are tapped. Lawkeeper will untap next turn and be available for its tap ability then.

annotations.description: Young Pyromancer (2/1) trades with Merfolk Pupil (1/1) — both die since Young Pyromancer only has 1 toughness. Young Pyromancer is a high-value card that generates tokens from future instants/sorceries, while Merfolk Pupil is just a 1/1 with its ETB already used. Saving 1 damage at 17 life is not worth sacrificing Young Pyromancer. Additionally, putting Merfolk Pupil in the graveyard gives the opponent access to its card filtering ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Merfolk Pupil with Young Pyromancer, trading both creatures
annotations.betterLine: Don't block — take the 1 damage and preserve Young Pyromancer for future token generation value

annotations.description: Passed the entire precombat main phase without taking any action. Failed to play Memorial to Genius (free land drop), and failed to deploy any creatures (Midnight Guard, Spectral Sailor, Faerie Vandal) while the opponent was almost completely tapped out. This wastes an entire turn of development with 5 untapped lands and multiple playable cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with no action, ending the turn with an unplayed land drop and multiple castable creatures in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Memorial to Genius as land drop, then cast Midnight Guard (2W) to develop the board while opponent is tapped out. Could also cast Spectral Sailor with remaining mana for additional board presence.

annotations.description: Cast Brightmare before playing their Plains land drop. With 4 untapped lands, casting Brightmare (3 mana) leaves only 1 mana open. Playing Plains first would give 5 lands, leaving 2 mana open after Brightmare, providing more flexibility for responses.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brightmare with 4 lands before making land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, then cast Brightmare, leaving 2 mana open instead of 1 (or 2 after postcombat land drop). Land-before-spell sequencing preserves maximum information and flexibility.

annotations.description: Targeted own Brightmare with its ETB tap ability instead of opponent's Gideon's Lawkeeper. Brightmare is summoning sick so tapping it is nearly meaningless (just +2 life). Tapping Gideon's Lawkeeper would neutralize its powerful tap ability for a turn cycle and still gain 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted own Brightmare, tapping it (while summoning sick) and gaining 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Target Gideon's Lawkeeper to tap it down, preventing it from using its tap ability to lock down MiniMx Worrier's attackers, while still gaining 1 life.

annotations.description: GPT5 Story timed out and failed to block the attacking Brightmare (2/3) with Midnight Guard (2/3). Blocking would have prevented 2 damage and left Brightmare at 1 toughness (vulnerable to removal/pings), while Midnight Guard would survive at 1 toughness. Since Midnight Guard has summoning sickness and can't attack anyway, blocking is essentially free.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) - took 2 damage from Brightmare unblocked.
annotations.betterLine: Block Brightmare with Midnight Guard. Both 2/3 creatures deal 2 damage to each other, both survive at 1 toughness. This prevents 2 damage and weakens the opponent's creature significantly.

annotations.description: MiniMx Worrier cast Faith's Fetters - a premium removal enchantment - targeting their own Thriving Bluff, which accomplishes almost nothing. Faith's Fetters doesn't even prevent mana abilities, so the land can still tap for mana. They gain 4 life but waste a powerful removal spell. The opponent has Gideon's Lawkeeper (which has been tapping down their creatures) and Midnight Guard as valid targets.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Faith's Fetters targeting own Thriving Bluff
annotations.betterLine: Save Faith's Fetters for an opponent's threatening permanent like Gideon's Lawkeeper (which has been disrupting attacks) or hold it for a future threat. Could have cast Distinguished Conjurer instead to develop the board.

annotations.description: All opponent creatures are tapped or have summoning sickness, meaning none can block. GPT5 Story passed up 3 free damage (or at minimum 2 from Midnight Guard). While keeping Gideon's Lawkeeper back to use its tap ability on the opponent's turn is defensible, Midnight Guard has no such utility and should have attacked for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures despite all opposing creatures being tapped/sick.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Midnight Guard for 2 unblockable damage. Attacking with both creatures for 3 damage was also likely correct since the Lawkeeper's tap ability may not be needed this cycle.

annotations.description: Attacked with Chandra's Magmutt alone, which either gets blocked and killed by Midnight Guard 2/3 or deals only 2 damage. More importantly, Magmutt's tap ability synergizes with Chandra's Pyreling (noncombat damage triggers double strike), making it the creature that should stay back untapped. Brightmare 2/3 or a multi-creature attack would pressure the opponent more effectively.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Magmutt untapped for its ping ability (which triggers Pyreling's double strike). Attack with Brightmare 2/3 and Chandra's Pyreling 1/3 instead - Lawkeeper can only tap one, and Midnight Guard can only block one, so at least one creature gets through. Then in second main, ping with Magmutt to potentially give Pyreling double strike for future turns' attacks.

annotations.description: Faerie Vandal has flying and the opponent has no flyers or reach creatures. It could attack for 1 guaranteed unblocked damage with zero risk. Not attacking with it wastes free damage, especially when behind on life 18-23.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Faerie Vandal for 1 free flying damage. Midnight Guard could also potentially attack profitably since Distinguished Conjurer is sick and can't block, leaving only Brightmare and Pyreling as blockers.

annotations.description: Attacking with Distinguished Conjurer (1/2) into potential blockers risks losing a creature with a valuable flicker ability ({4}{W}, {T}: exile and return a creature). The opponent has Midnight Guard and Faerie Vandal available to block, and the Conjurer likely trades with Faerie Vandal or dies to Midnight Guard for minimal value.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all three creatures including Distinguished Conjurer
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Brightmare and Chandra's Pyreling, keeping Distinguished Conjurer back to preserve its activated flicker ability for future turns. The Conjurer's ability to repeatedly blink Brightmare (tapping creatures and gaining life) is more valuable than the 1 damage it might deal.

annotations.description: Failed to assign any blockers against three attackers, taking 4 damage unnecessarily. Critically, Midnight Guard 2/3 could block and trade with Brightmare 2/3, and Magnanimous Magistrate (with 4 reprieve counters) would return the Midnight Guard to play since its mana value is 3. This would eliminate an opponent's key creature for free.
annotations.actionTaken: No blocks assigned (timeout/no response), taking 4 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Brightmare with Midnight Guard. The trade kills Brightmare, and Magnanimous Magistrate's ability returns Midnight Guard to play (removing 3 reprieve counters). This eliminates an opposing threat at no real cost. Could also consider blocking Distinguished Conjurer with Faerie Vandal for a mutual trade.

annotations.description: Failed to assign any blockers against three attacking creatures, taking 4 unnecessary damage. The opponent was mostly tapped out (only 1 untapped Plains), making combat tricks unlikely. Midnight Guard could have blocked and killed Distinguished Conjurer (surviving), and Magnanimous Magistrate could have blocked and killed Brightmare (surviving). This would have eliminated two threats while only taking 1 damage from Chandra's Pyreling.
annotations.actionTaken: No blockers assigned (timeout/no response), taking 4 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Brightmare with Magnanimous Magistrate (kills it, Magistrate survives) and block Distinguished Conjurer with Midnight Guard (kills it, Guard survives). Only take 1 damage from Pyreling instead of 4, while killing two opposing creatures.
